CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE M.I.ARUN  ORAL ORDER 1.

Aggrieved by the order passed in LAC No.22/2017 dated 23.11.2018 by the Principal Senior Civil Judge and CJM, Mysuru, wherein, the petition filed by the respondent herein / claimant therein under Section 18(3)(b) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 (for short, 'the LA Act') has been allowed

,
the present writ petition is filed.
2. The lands of the respondent have been acquired for the purposes of Karnataka Industrial Areas Development NC: 2024:KHC:37971 Board (for short, 'the KIADB').

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The contention of the petitioner is that a consent award as contemplated under Section 29(2) of the Karnataka Industrial Areas Development Act (for short, 'the KIAD Act') has been passed.
It is submitted that in spite of passing of the consent award, as the respondent did not come forward to receive the same, it has been deposited before the Reference Court.
Thus, it is contended that the respondent herein is entitled to receive the said compensation upon proving that she is the owner of the property.

As there is no award passed as contemplated under Section 29(3) of the KIAD Act read with Section 11 of the LA Act, 1894, the petitioner could not have maintained the petition under Section 18(3) (Karnataka Amendment) of the LA Act.
It is submitted that the Civil Court has no jurisdiction to entertain such an application.

It is further submitted that in spite of it, the Reference Court has erroneously entertained the petition filed by the respondent and has treated the compensation received by the respondent as NC: 2024:KHC:37971 one that is under protest and it is hearing the matter to determine whether the compensation deposited is sufficient or not.
For the said reasons, the present writ petition is filed with a prayer to set aside the impugned order.
3. Per contra, the respondent justifies the order passed by the trial Court.
She contends that she never gave the consent to accept the amount determined by the petitioner-SLAO and she has

sentences.text:
The question that arises for consideration is under the given facts and circumstances of the case is, can it be considered that there was a valid consent award passed by the petitioner or that the amount deposited before the Reference Court by the KIADB has to be treated as a general award deposited before the Reference Court.
NC: 2024:KHC:37971 5. Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act reads as under:-
"29. Compensation:
(x) (2). Where the amount of compensation has been determined by agreement between the State Government and the person to be compensated, it shall be paid in accordance with such agreement."
6.

Thus, under a consent award, there is no dispute as to the ownership of the property or the persons interested in the property or the apportionment of compensation amount to the persons interested or the amount to be paid for acquiring the said property.
Under such circumstances, the petitioner-SLAO is required to directly disburse the compensation amount in favour of the person interested directly.

Only when the SLAO is not in a position to determine the ownership of the property or the persons interested in the property and their respective shares over the property or when there is a dispute with regard to the ownership, the SLAO not being competent to NC:
2024:KHC:37971 decide interse dispute between the parties concerned or as to who is the owner of the property concerned, is required to pass a general award and deposit the same before the Reference Court.

In the instant case, the respondent contends that without issuance of any notice about the acquisition of the property or determination of the compensation, the amount has been deposited before the Reference Court.

Though the petitioner-SLAO contends that the respondent was notified as to the determination of the award, it is not in dispute that the respondent did not come forward to accept the same, which constrained the petitioner-SLAO to deposit the same before the Reference Court.
In short, there has been no valid acceptance by the respondent, of the offer made by the petitioner regarding the compensation awarded for acquiring the land.

Thus, under the circumstances, it has to be concluded that there has been no consent award passed as under Section 29(2) of the KIAD Act and the award under deposit has to be considered as a general NC:
2024:KHC:37971 award and under such circumstances, the land losers are always at liberty to seek for a compensation which is just fair and reasonable according to him.
7.
For the aforementioned reason, I do not see any error in the order passed by the trial Court and the Writ Petition is accordingly dismissed.
